record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Computational Geometry
record.original_question: In the rectangular-domain shrinking-barrier problem for unit disks, the point s lies above all disks, the point t lies below all disks, paths are restricted to a vertical slab containing s and t, and each disk may be shrunk by an individually chosen amount. The objective is to minimize the total amount of shrinking required to allow an s-t path that avoids the shrunk disks. Although an approximation scheme is known for this rectangular-domain problem, determine whether the exact optimization problem is NP-hard, and settle its computational complexity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let R be an axis-aligned rectangular region in the plane. Inside R is placed a finite family D = {D_1, …, D_n} of closed unit disks (the "barriers"). Two points s and t are given such that s lies strictly above every disk of D and t lies strictly below every disk of D, and both s and t belong to a vertical slab (a strip bounded by two vertical lines) that contains them; all candidate paths from s to t are required to remain inside this vertical slab.

Shrinking. For each disk D_i, one may choose a real number r_i with 0 ≤ r_i ≤ 1 and replace D_i by the concentric closed disk D_i' of radius 1 − r_i (so r_i is the "amount of shrinking" applied to D_i; r_i = 1 means the disk is removed). The total cost of a shrinking is Σ_{i=1}^{n} r_i.

Problem. Determine the minimum value of Σ r_i over all choices (r_1, …, r_n) ∈ [0,1]^n such that there exists a continuous path from s to t, lying in the vertical slab and inside R, that avoids the interior of every shrunk disk D_i'.

Question. Although a polynomial-time approximation scheme is known for this optimization problem, the exact decision version (given a threshold τ, is the minimum total shrinking at most τ?) has unsettled complexity. Decide whether this exact problem is NP-hard, and, more generally, classify its computational complexity.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches on barrier resilience for unit disks indicate that the exact complexity of the (rectangular-domain) variant remains unresolved: known results include PTAS/FPT algorithms and approximation guarantees, and NP-hardness is established only for related fat-region or rectangle-with-aspect-ratio variants, not for unit disks in this shrinking formulation. No published proof of NP-hardness or polynomial-time exact algorithm for the shrinking unit-disk version was found.

status_evidence.snippet: The complexity of barrier resilience for unit disk barriers is an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The exact complexity for unit disks is open.

status_evidence.title: On the Complexity of Barrier Resilience for Fat Regions and Bounded Ply
status_evidence.snippet: NP-hard for fat regions with bounded ply (axis-aligned rectangles of aspect ratio 1:(1+ε)); PTAS and FPT results for unit disks.
status_evidence.claim: NP-hardness is known only for fat-region variants, not the unit-disk case.
